name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah near its record low at about 18,200 per dollar on 13 Nov despite intervention; no EM default or IMF rescue
state: Indonesia's rupiah neared its record low of 18,279 per dollar on 12 Nov and ended 13 Nov near 18,200, down about 1.1% on the week, as a strong dollar, political uncertainty and expected index-related outflows weighed; Bank Indonesia has intervened and meets the week of 16 Nov (Trading Economics). The Turkish lira has traded near a record of about 50 per dollar since 3 Nov in a managed depreciation. Neither has fallen 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy in default, under capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 16 Nov.
for_you: Businesses and travellers dealing in Indonesian rupiah or Turkish lira are exposed to further currency swings. Holders of emerging-market funds are exposed to outflows while the dollar is strong.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month, no default or IMF emergency request: Normal

sources.title: Trading Economics — Rupiah weakens as dollar firms and political risks mount
Trading Economics — Turkish lira holds at record lows

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
